chunks: From him, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Ubayd ibn Zur'arah, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who prays the morning prayer one rak'ah, then sits for the tashahhud, then departs and leaves, then returns, and then remembers afterwards that he had only prayed one rak'ah. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He adds one rak'ah to it.'

So there is no contradiction between these two reports and the first report which we presented from Ammar al-Sabati, and between the first reports, because the way in these reports is to interpret them as meaning that when he departs and leaves and returns without facing away from the qiblah, it is permissible for him at that time to build upon what has passed. And the first reports are interpreted as meaning that when he faces away from the qiblah, it becomes obligatory upon him to restart the prayer. So there is no contradiction between them in any case.
And that which adds clarification to that is what he narrated:

key_terms.اَلْبِنَاءُ عَلَى مَا مَضَى: building upon what has passed (continuing the previous prayer)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if I realize I only prayed one rak'ah after leaving the prayer area?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the fiqh of *sahw* (forgetfulness) by distinguishing between minor and major disruptions in prayer based on orientation to the qiblah. It demonstrates the Shia scholarly method of reconciling seemingly contradictory reports by contextualizing the physical actions of the worshipper, ensuring that the validity of the prayer is preserved unless a significant break occurs. This ruling emphasizes the importance of maintaining spiritual continuity during worship while providing practical flexibility for common human error.
